newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight rates fail to inspire, orders cited.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight rates fail to inspire, orders cited.

text.p: The sugar freight market saw a number of fixtures on routine runs on Wednesday but there was little improvement in reported rates, shipbrokers said.
CSR fixed 16,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Japan for mid-December at $19.00, which shipbrokers said was $2.00 lower than the rate achieved for the last similar fixture.
CSR entered the market with another order for the same run with an increased size of 18,000 tonnes for 1/10 January.

Mauritius Sugar Syndicate was thought to have fixed 14,500 tonnes on its usual run from Port Louis to London for 19/23 December at just under stg 14.00, a touch higher than last time. E D & F Man was said to have fixed a prompt 6/7,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Santander to the Turkish Mediterranean.

Tate & Lyle revised its earlier order from Maputo to London for mid-December dates, raising the size to 15/16,500 tonnes. Jean Lion quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from north Brazil to Syria plus various options for 10/13 December. Louis Dreyfus was active on the market on Wednesday, issuing two orders out of Puerto Quetzal for mid-December. It quoted for 24,000 tonnes to US Gulf/Atlantic and 14/14,700 tonnes to Chile. Lastly, shipbrokers said Czarnikow Rionda was open for a 14,000-tonne bagged cargo from south Brazil to Mediterranean with west Africa and Red Sea for end December/early January.
